title: Serial Cashback Refinancers - How did you do it?
body:
O.P.
this post was edited
[Mortgage Brokers and Virtue Signallers – Please stop here]
Opening up this thread to have informative and frank discussion amongst cashback hungry refinancers.
Wanting to understand - (1) How much did you collect (net of fees and excess interest over say last 12 months) (2) How frequently do you refinance (3) Do you combine your properties in single applications (where allowed) or prefer separate simultaneous applications (4) With cashback amounts and numbers of lenders offering them dwindling – what are your planning for 2022?
About me -
Collected $12,000 (~$10k net of fees and excess interest) across two properties over last 12 months dealing directly with banks (Investment ANZ->Westpac; OO Westpac->CBA->BoM). Currently in process with Citibank for their $6k (>$1M lending OO) and HSBC for their $3,288 Cashback (Inv) and hoping to settle by Feb’22. Once settled, will start refinancing process with ING ($3k) for investment and RAMS($4k) for OO.
In terms of timeframe between refinances, I did 'Investment ANZ->Westpac’ process ~11 months ago and still with them as got great rate, started 'OO Westpac->CBA’ refinance process the very day property settled with Westpac(new purchase) in June’21 and moved to CBA within 2 months. Started CBA->BoM process 2 weeks after settlement with CBA and moved my loan to BoM next month. FASTRefi® FTW.
Plans for 2022 – Will keep churning as long as banks allow, no one has seriously objected till now and no credit score impact as all of these were HL enquiries. Once exhausted, will move to TicToc/Homestar at 1.89/1.79% OO variable rate and will find cheapest IO variable rate for investment and just leave them there till next wave of cashbacks start.
Edit – Spellings.

---- replies ----
[User #4158911756 postssp00kerWhirlpool Forums Addict] Buzzinga666 writes...
Collected $12,000 (~$10k net of fees and excess interest) across two properties over last 12 months dealing directly with banks (Investment ANZ->Westpac; OO Westpac->CBA->BoM)
That's pretty impressive. I doubt you'll find many people doing better than you.
Were you able to get a lower interest rate with each refinance or was it the same?
just leave them there till next wave of cashbacks start.
Will be interesting to see how the cashbacks hold up, once interest rates start rising. It feels like the cashbacks became more extravagant over the past 2 years, with low interest rates. It seems to be a way for lenders to lure borrowers, without reducing rates further. Once rates go up, perhaps lenders will start competing on rates again.
[User #31146203 postsxfilesForum Regular] I did anz 4k, boq 3k, St george 4k cashbacks over last 2 yrs. 2yr Fixed rates were lower than what I was getting in each case. Had mortgage broker involved so they did all the leg work...
[User #5211721062 postsPete010Whirlpool Enthusiast] Buzzinga666 writes...
Currently in process with Citibank for their $6k
I note this is paid over 2 years – $3k year one, $3k year two so this will slow the plans down a bit?
Personally only received cash back once, it’s not something I would have the patience to make a career from :)
[User #84969696 postsBuzzinga666Participant] O.P.
sp00ker writes...
Were you able to get a lower interest rate with each refinance or was it the same?
Yes – For OO refinances, I always moved between fixed rates i.e. Westpac 1.94%>CBA1.94%>BoM 1.89%
Never had to pay break fee as was told bank wholesale rates haven’t lowered in last year.
Pete010 writes...
I note this is paid over 2 years – $3k year one, $3k year two so this will slow the plans down a bit?
That’s not what I have been told. All of it is paid 60 days after settlement.
it’s not something I would have the patience to make a career from :)
I feel you. It’s actually a test of patience, though it’s not bad to get $3k-$4k after-tax cash boost for couple hours keyboard/phone work if you keep your documents organised. I think of it as temporary side hustle :)
[User #194294551 postsdbamhWhirlpool Enthusiast] xfiles writes...
I did anz 4k, boq 3k, St george 4k cashbacks over last 2 yrs. 2yr Fixed rates were lower than what I was getting in each case. Had mortgage broker involved so they did all the leg work...
Does the broker basically work for free if you switch banks so quickly?
[User #31146203 postsxfilesForum Regular] dbamh writes...
Does the broker basically work for free if you switch banks so quickly?
Different loans so they get their commission too.
[User #84969696 postsBuzzinga666Participant] O.P.
Didn’t he/she object to too many refinances and thus clawback of upfront by previous bank? I understand he will get paid out same amount from new bank and keep the trail.
Is he happy with 2-3 month subsequent refinance timeframe?
[User #31146203 postsxfilesForum Regular] Buzzinga666 writes...
Didn’t he/she object to too many refinances and thus clawback of upfront by previous bank?
It's for different loans / properties. With a broker you are kind of locked in for 2 yrs which is fine if the loan is fixed at 2 yrs.
[User #786244192 postswisejsWhirlpool Forums Addict] Did it twice in 2022, only about 2months a part. Approx $6200 net for ~2-3hours work. Credit score went up.
Will try at least once this year.
[User #592500219 postsTrickeeForum Regular] Does anyone know of any cash backs for loans <$250k – I'm seeing this is a minimum everywhere I'm trying
[User #806642638 postsJb88Whirlpool Enthusiast] Same as you OP. pocketd about 10k over there last 18 months. 4k from NAB. Then 4k from St George. Then 4k from Suncorp. Now I’m with Athena on 1.89%. Hard to refinance away from that. Most of the offers are only 3k at the moment. I would do it again for at least 4k to a decent rate.
[User #1803452448 posts24CarrotsWhirlpool Forums Addict] Trickee writes...
I'm seeing this is a minimum everywhere I'm trying
Yeah I’m the same, except my loan size is 350k, but my offset is 250k. Many of them are saying “net of offset” to be eligible.
[User #806642638 postsJb88Whirlpool Enthusiast] Buzzinga666 writes...
Have you tried RAMS $4k?
I haven’t. I wasn’t really committed to anything before so it was easy to refi. I feel like Athena is pretty decent at the moment. I just churned an ANZ credit card offer which gave me 900$ in gift cards after using for only three months without paying a dollar interest. There’s plenty of easy money to be hustled if you’re willing.
[User #116579170 postsHeartstarterForum Regular] Here I am thinking I beat the man scoring 2x $2000 cashback on two new loans I never paid a cent from cause I drew them into the offset accounts in full. You guys are next level!
[User #30154582 postsD is Keypiuq gnisumaWhirlpool Enthusiast] For me, in the last 2 years: WBC to ANZ – 3k ANZ to WBC – 3k Was closed to moving to another bank recently (settlement booked) but got a retention offer to match rates and cashback – another 3k.
For those currently with WBC considering moving, I'd suggest getting in touch with their retention team. They're basically paying to keep you!
